Figure 1:Sauron architecture.Two lightweight planning steps cluster the rubric criteriaCCby
likely shared evidence and produce an advisory task gistgg. Each cluster runs as a parallel
investigation session. The investigator reaches the traceτ\tauand stateSSthrough bounded queries
and proposes claims. The evidence verifier checks each claim against its source, records the result in
the session’s evidence store, and returns rejected claims with a reason. The investigator separately proposes
verdicts, and the verdict finalizer accepts one only when verified claims support it. Each criterion receives
its own verdict and a receipt of the evidence it cites.

Figure 2:Investigation through bounded queries.Three criteria from one episode
(51 events, 19 tool calls), investigated in one session.
(a) Two state reads suffice for the outcome criterion.
(b) The consistency criterion reads both sources and finds that the saved Amazon total differs from the retrieved one.
(c) The process criterion is answerable only from the trace. The investigator reuses the Chase lookup found in (b),
locates the reporting event, and confirms that the lookup came first. Each read is tagged broad or targeted, and each panel ends with the claims the investigator proposes for verification.

Figure 3:Evidence verification.Each proposed atoma=(x,t,ℓ)a=(x,t,\ell), with claimxx, evidence typett, and
locatorℓ\ell, is checked against the source content retrieved fromℓ\ell. An exact claim (a1a_{1})
is compared mechanically with the stored value. An interpretive claim (a2a_{2}) goes to an isolated
faithfulness checker that sees only the claim and the cited passage.
A claim whose source cannot be retrieved (a3a_{3}) is rejected without verification,
and the reason is returned to the investigator.
